p.src: Now Zhu Tong said to the others, “If you want me to go up the mountain, then kill the Black Whirlwind and let me vent my anger. Only then will I let the matter rest.” Li Kui flew into a rage when he heard this. “You can bite my arse! I was acting under the orders of Brothers Chao and Song. What the hell has it got to do with me?” Zhu Tong’s fury flared, and once again he tried to fight Li Kui, but the other three restrained them. Zhu Tong said, “So long as the Black Whirlwind is there, I will not go up the mountain even if it costs me my life!” Chai Jin said, “That is easily settled. I have a plan: simply leave Brother Li here with me. You three can go up the mountain and thereby fulfill the wishes of Lords Chao and Song.” Zhu Tong said, “Now that this deed has been done, the prefect will certainly send official papers to Yuncheng County ordering my arrest and the seizure of my family. What am I to do?” Scholar Wu said, “Set your mind at ease. By now Song Gongming has most likely brought your honored family safely to the mountain.” Only then did Zhu Tong feel somewhat reassured. Chai Jin laid out wine to entertain them and saw them off that very day. Toward evening, the three took their leave of Lord Chai and departed. Chai Jin ordered his retainers to saddle three horses and escort them beyond the pass. As they parted, Wu Yong again warned Li Kui, “Be careful. Stay here at His Lordship’s estate for a while, and on no account stir up trouble and implicate others. After three or six months, when his temper has cooled, we will come and take you back to the mountain. He will very likely invite Lord Chai to join us as well.” The three mounted their horses and rode away.

p.src: We shall say no more of Chai Jin and Li Kui returning to the estate, but speak instead of Zhu Tong accompanying Wu Yong and Lei Heng to join the band at Liangshan Marsh. After traveling some distance, they passed beyond the borders of Cangzhou, whereupon the estate retainers mounted their horses and returned. The three took the road toward Liangshan Marsh, and nothing of note occurred along the way. Before long they reached Zhu Gui’s tavern and first sent someone up to notify the stronghold. Chao Gai and Song Jiang led all the chiefs, great and small, beating drums and playing flutes as they came all the way to Golden Sands Beach to welcome them. There the entire company exchanged greetings. They all mounted horses, returned to the main stronghold atop the mountain, and dismounted before it. Then they gathered in the Hall of Righteous Assembly and spoke of old times. Zhu Tong said, “Now that I have been summoned to the mountain, the prefect of Cangzhou will certainly send official papers to Yuncheng County ordering the arrest of my family. What am I to do?” Song Jiang laughed heartily. “Be at ease, elder brother. Your good wife and son were brought here many days ago.” Zhu Tong asked, “Where are they now?” Song Jiang replied, “They are being cared for at my father’s quarters. Go and see how they fare, brother.” Zhu Tong was overjoyed. Song Jiang had someone lead Zhu Tong straight to Song Taigong’s quarters, where he found his entire family, together with all their valuables and luggage. His wife said, “Some days ago, a man brought a letter saying that you had already joined the stronghold. So we packed our belongings and hurried here through the night.” Zhu Tong went out and bowed his thanks to everyone. Song Jiang then had Zhu Tong and Lei Heng establish their quarters on the mountaintop, while banquets were held for several days to celebrate the new chiefs. Of this there is no more to tell.

p.src: Meanwhile, when evening came and Zhu Tong had not returned carrying the young master, the prefect of Cangzhou sent men searching in every direction until midnight. The next day someone found the boy slain in the woods and reported it to the prefect. When the prefect heard, he flew into a rage. He went personally to inspect the woods and wept without cease, then prepared a coffin and had the body cremated. The next day he convened court and immediately dispatched official documents throughout the region, ordering the pursuit and arrest of Zhu Tong himself. Yuncheng County had already reported that Zhu Tong’s wife had fled with the whole family and that their whereabouts were unknown. Notices were circulated to every prefecture and county offering a reward for their capture. Of this there is no more to tell.

p.src: When Chai Jin saw Chai Huangcheng, he sat down beside his uncle’s couch and wailed aloud in grief. Huangcheng’s second wife came out and consoled him. “Your Lordship has endured the dust and hardship of the road. You have only just arrived, so please do not grieve so deeply.” After Chai Jin had paid his respects, he asked what had happened. The second wife replied, “The newly appointed prefect here, Gao Lian, also commands this prefecture’s troops. He is a paternal cousin of Grand Marshal Gao in the Eastern Capital, and relying on his kinsman’s power, he does whatever he pleases here. He brought with him a brother of his wife named Yin Tianxi, whom everyone calls Director Yin. That rogue is still young, but he too relies on the authority of his brother-in-law Gao Lian and runs rampant here, harming the people. Some fawning busybody told him that behind our residence stood a splendidly built garden with a pavilion over the water. That rogue brought twenty or thirty men, each more treacherous than the last, forced his way into our home, and inspected the rear of the property. He then ordered us to leave, saying he meant to live here himself. Huangcheng said to him, ‘Our house is of imperial blood, and at our gate we possess an iron certificate inscribed in cinnabar, bestowed by the former dynasty. No one is permitted to bully us. How dare you seize my residence? Where do you expect me to send my old and young?’ The rogue would hear none of it and insisted that we vacate the house. When Huangcheng tried to seize hold of him, the rogue instead shoved and beat him. The outrage made him ill. He took to his bed and never rose, refusing food, while every medicine proved useless. Plainly he is far from heaven but close to the grave. Now that Your Lordship has come home to take charge, even if the worst should happen, I need no longer fear.” Chai Jin replied, “Set your mind at ease, honored aunt. Please concentrate on finding a good physician to treat my uncle. As for protecting the household, I shall send someone back to my home in Cangzhou to fetch the iron certificate inscribed in cinnabar, and then I will settle matters with him. Even if I must bring the complaint before the authorities and His Present Majesty himself, I do not fear him!” The second wife said, “Huangcheng is utterly incapable of managing affairs. Your Lordship is indeed the one who can argue our case properly.”

p.src: After looking in on his uncle for a while, Chai Jin came out and told Li Kui and the men who had accompanied him every detail. When Li Kui heard this, he sprang to his feet and cried, “What an outrageous scoundrel! I have my great axes here. Let him taste a few blows from them, and then we can talk.” Chai Jin said, “Brother Li, calm your anger. Why needlessly descend to violence with him? Though he relies on his power to bully others, my family possesses an imperial edict of protection. We cannot reason with him here, but in the capital there are men far greater than he, and the statutes stand plainly written. We shall take him to court.” Li Kui said, “Statutes, statutes! If they were ever obeyed, the realm would never have fallen into disorder! My way is to strike first and talk afterward. If that scoundrel goes to lodge a complaint, I will chop down every one of those damned officials as well.” Chai Jin laughed. “No wonder Zhu Tong wants to fight you and cannot bear to meet you. This is within an imperial city. How can you compare it to running wild in your little stronghold?” Li Kui said, “What of it if it is an imperial city? Did I somehow refrain from killing men in Jiangzhou and Wuwei Army?” Chai Jin said, “Let me first see how matters develop. If I have need of you, Brother, I shall ask for your help. Until then, please remain quietly in your room.” While they were speaking, a concubine hurried out from within to summon the young master to attend Lord Chai.

p.src: Chai Jin went inside to the couch and saw Lord Chai lying there with tears in his eyes. He said to Chai Jin, “Worthy nephew, you are a man of lofty spirit and have brought no disgrace upon our ancestors. Today Yin Tianxi has beaten me to death. For the sake of our kinship, take my letter to the capital yourself, intercept the imperial procession, and present my grievance. Avenge me, and even beneath the Nine Springs I shall be grateful for your devotion as my nephew. Take care! Take care! I have nothing more to charge you with!” With those words, he breathed his last. Chai Jin wept bitterly for a long while. His uncle’s second wife, fearing that he would faint, managed to soothe him and said, “Young Master, there will be time enough for grief. For now, let us discuss the funeral arrangements.” Chai Jin said, “The covenant is at my home, for I did not bring it with me. I must send someone through the night to fetch it, so that I may take it to the Eastern Capital and lodge a complaint. For now, prepare coffins for my uncle’s honored spirit and enshroud his body. Once we have donned mourning dress, we shall discuss what to do next.” Chai Jin ordered inner and outer coffins prepared according to official regulations and the spirit tablet arranged in accordance with the rites. The whole household donned deep mourning, and high and low alike raised their lamentations. Outside, Li Kui heard weeping in the hall. He clenched his fists and rubbed his palms in fury, but when he questioned the attendants, none would tell him what had happened. The household invited monks to conduct meritorious rites for the dead.

p.src: Before long, more than two hundred men appeared, each armed with sword, staff, spear, or cudgel, and surrounded Chai Huangcheng’s house. Seeing that they had come to make an arrest, Chai Jin stepped forward and said, “I will go with you to the prefectural office and state my case.” The men first bound Chai Jin, then entered the house and searched for the huge black fellow who had committed the killing. Unable to find him, they took only Chai Jin, bound, to the prefectural court and forced him to kneel before the hall. The prefect Gao Lian had heard that his brother-in-law Yin Tianxi had been beaten to death. He sat in the hall grinding his teeth in fury, waiting only for the culprit to be brought before him. Chai Jin was promptly shoved to the ground below the steps, and Gao Lian shouted, “How dare you beat my Yin Tianxi to death?” Chai Jin pleaded, “I am a direct descendant of Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou, and my family possesses the former dynasty’s iron certificate bearing Emperor Taizu’s sworn pledge. I now reside in Cangzhou. Because my uncle Chai Huangcheng was gravely ill, I came especially to visit him. Regrettably, he died, and his coffin now lies at home awaiting burial. Court Attendant Yin brought twenty or thirty men to the house and insisted on driving us out. Refusing to let me explain, he ordered his men to beat us. p.src: Now Li Kui traveled through the night back to the Liangshan Marsh. Reaching the stronghold, he went to see the assembled chieftains. The moment Zhu Tong saw Li Kui, anger surged within him. Drawing a broad-bladed sword, he charged straight at Li Kui. The Black Whirlwind pulled out his twin axes and met Zhu Tong in combat. Chao Gai, Song Jiang, and all the other chieftains rushed forward together and restrained them. Song Jiang apologized to Zhu Tong, saying, “The young prefect’s son was killed before, but that was not Li Kui’s doing of his own accord. It was the plan devised at the time by our strategist, Scholar Wu, because you, elder brother, refused our invitation to come up the mountain. Now that you have come to the stronghold, do not harbor it in your heart. Let us work together with one purpose to advance our righteous cause, and give no outsiders cause to mock us.” He then told brother Li Kui to apologize to Zhu Tong. Li Kui glared with his strange eyes and cried out, “How can he put on such airs? I have often exerted myself for this stronghold, while he has not performed the slightest service. Why should I be made to apologize to him?” Song Jiang said, “Brother, you were the one who killed the young prefect’s son. Though you acted under the strategist’s strict command, Zhu Tong is also your elder in age. For my sake, bow and apologize to him; afterward, I myself shall bow to you.” Unable to withstand Song Jiang’s pleading, Li Kui said, “I am not afraid of you. But since my elder brother presses me, I have no choice. I will apologize to you.” Pressed by Song Jiang, Li Kui had no choice but to cast aside his twin axes and bow twice to Zhu Tong. Only then did Zhu Tong’s anger subside. Chief Chao then ordered a banquet prepared in the stronghold to reconcile the two men.

p.src: Li Kui related how Lord Chai had gone to Gaotangzhou to visit his sick uncle Chai Huangcheng, only for Yin Tianxi, the brother-in-law of Prefect Gao, to try to seize the house and garden and to strike and abuse Chai Jin. “So I beat that wretch Yin Tianxi to death.” When Song Jiang had heard him out, he exclaimed in alarm, “By running away yourself, you must have implicated Lord Chai and embroiled him in a criminal case!” Scholar Wu said, “Do not be alarmed, elder brother. When Dai Zong returns to the mountain, we shall know what has happened.” Li Kui asked, “Where has brother Dai Zong gone?” Wu Yong replied, “I feared you would cause serious trouble at Lord Chai’s estate, so I specially sent him to summon you back to the mountain. When he arrived and failed to find you, he surely went to Gaotangzhou in search of you.” Before he had finished speaking, a junior officer came to report that Superintendent Dai had returned. Song Jiang went out to welcome him. Once they were seated in the hall, he immediately asked about Lord Chai. Dai Zong replied, “When I reached Lord Chai’s estate, I learned that he and Li Kui had already gone to Gaotangzhou. I hurried straight there to make inquiries, only to hear everyone in the city saying that Yin Tianxi, while disputing possession of Chai Huangcheng’s estate, had been beaten to death by a huge black fellow. Lord Chai has now been implicated, cast into bonds, and confined in prison. Every member of Chai Huangcheng’s household has been seized, and all the family property confiscated and sealed. Lord Chai’s life may be lost at any moment.” Chao Gai said, “That black wretch has done it again! Wherever he goes, he stirs up trouble.” Li Kui said, “They injured Chai Huangcheng, who died from pent-up rage, then came to seize his house and ordered Lord Chai beaten. Even a living Buddha could not have endured it!” Chao Gai said, “Lord Chai has always shown kindness to our stronghold. Now that he is in peril, how can we fail to descend the mountain and rescue him? I will make the journey myself.” Song Jiang said, “Elder brother, you are the master of the stronghold. I am willing to descend the mountain in your place.” Scholar Wu said, “Though the city of Gaotangzhou is small, its population is dense, its troops numerous, and its provisions abundant. We must not underestimate the enemy. Let us ask the twelve chieftains Lin Chong, Hua Rong, Qin Ming, Li Jun, Lü Fang, Guo Sheng, Sun Li, Ou Peng, Yang Lin, Deng Fei, Ma Lin, and Bai Sheng to command five thousand horse and foot as the advance vanguard. p.src: Prefect Gao Lian personally led the three hundred Divine Troops. Clad in armor with a sword on his back, he mounted his horse and rode outside the city. He arrayed his officers in a formation around him and placed the three hundred Divine Troops in the center. Flags waved, men shouted, drums thundered, and gongs rang as they waited for the enemy to arrive. Meanwhile, Lin Chong, Hua Rong, and Qin Ming arrived at the head of five thousand troops. The two armies met, their banners and drums facing one another, and each side used powerful bows and heavy crossbows to secure the foot of its formation. War horns sounded within both armies, and the battle drums began to roll. Hua Rong and Qin Ming, accompanied by ten chieftains, rode to the front and reined in their horses. The chieftain Lin Chong leveled his eighteen-foot Serpent Spear, spurred his horse out of the ranks, and shouted fiercely, “Whoever is ready to die in Gaotang Prefecture, come forth!” Gao Lian urged his horse forward and led more than thirty officers out beneath the command banner. Reining in, he pointed at Lin Chong and cursed, “You death-blind rebels! How dare you invade my city?” Lin Chong shouted, “You brigand who preys upon the people! Sooner or later I shall fight my way to the capital and hack that treacherous minister Gao Qiu, who deceives his sovereign, into ten thousand pieces. Only then will my desire be satisfied!” Gao Lian flew into a rage and turned to ask, “Who will ride out first and seize this bandit?” From among the officers emerged a troop controller surnamed Yu and named Zhi. He whipped his horse forward, brandishing his saber, and charged straight out before the lines. At the sight of him, Lin Chong charged straight at Yu Zhi. Before they had exchanged five bouts, Lin Chong drove his Serpent Spear into Yu Zhi’s chest, sending him tumbling head over heels from his horse. Gao Lian was greatly alarmed at the sight. “Who else will ride out and avenge him?” Another troop controller emerged from among the officers. His surname was Wen and his given name Wenbao. Wielding a long spear and riding a yellow-dun horse, he came swiftly before the lines, his bridle bells ringing and his ornaments chiming; The four hooves of his horse churned up the dust of war as he charged straight at Lin Chong. Seeing this, Qin Ming shouted, “Brother, rest a while and watch me behead this villain at once!” Lin Chong reined in his horse, withdrew his tempered-steel spear, and yielded the fight against Wen Wenbao to Qin Ming. After the two had fought for more than ten bouts, Qin Ming deliberately left an opening and let his opponent thrust in with the spear. Then, with one swift lift and fall of his mace, he sliced away half of Wen Wenbao’s skull. Wen died in the saddle, while his horse ran back to its own lines. The soldiers in both opposing formations raised a deafening shout together.

The city gates were opened, the drawbridge lowered, and the army came forth and formed its battle lines. Song Jiang rode out before the lines with sword in hand. Seeing a cluster of black banners in Gao Lian’s army, Scholar Wu said, “The troops beneath those black banners are the ones who perform the ‘Divine Masters’ Stratagem.’ But if they employ that art again, how are we to meet them?” Song Jiang said, “Do not worry, Strategist. I have my own method for breaking their formation. Let none of our officers or soldiers be frightened or doubtful. Think only of pressing forward and attacking.” Gao Lian instructed all his officers, high and low, “Do not challenge them to individual contests. As soon as you hear the plaque sound, join forces and seize Song Jiang together. I shall reward you handsomely.” As the battle cries rose from both armies, Gao Lian rode before the lines. Hanging from his saddle bow was the bronze Beast-Gathering Plaque, inscribed with dragon patterns and phoenix seals, and in his hand he held his precious sword. Song Jiang pointed at Gao Lian and cursed, “I was not here last night, and my brothers mistakenly lost a battle. p.src: At the sound of Gao Lian's bronze tablet, a swarm of monstrous beasts and venomous creatures charged straight at them, leaving all the men and horses in Song Jiang's ranks petrified. Song Jiang cast aside his sword, wheeled his horse around, and fled first. The chieftains crowded around him, and all fled for their lives. Officers and soldiers alike could no longer look out for one another, but scrambled for any road of escape. Behind them, Gao Lian swept his sword forward; with the spirit soldiers in front and the government troops behind, they fell upon the fugitives together. Song Jiang's army suffered a crushing defeat. Gao Lian pursued and slew them for more than twenty li before sounding the gong to recall his troops and returning to the city. When Song Jiang reached the foot of an earthen slope, he halted and gathered his forces and established a stockaded camp. Though some soldiers had been lost, he was relieved that all the chieftains were safe. After settling the troops, he consulted his strategist Wu Yong: “In this assault on Gaotang Prefecture we have now lost two battles in succession. We have no means of overcoming those spirit soldiers. What are we to do?” Scholar Wu replied, “If that scoundrel can employ this ‘Stratagem of the Divine Host,’ he is certain to raid our camp tonight. We can devise a plan in advance against him. Only a small force should remain encamped here, while the rest of us withdraw to our former camp.” Song Jiang gave orders that only Yang Lin and Bai Sheng were to remain and guard the camp; all the other troops withdrew to the former camp to rest.

p.src: That night wind and thunder raged. As Yang Lin and Bai Sheng watched from the grass with more than three hundred men, they saw Gao Lian approach on foot at the head of three hundred spirit soldiers, whistling up the wind as they charged into the camp. Finding it deserted, they immediately turned to leave. Yang Lin and Bai Sheng raised a great shout. Fearing he had fallen into a trap, Gao Lian fled in haste, while the three hundred spirit soldiers scattered in every direction. Yang Lin and Bai Sheng loosed their crossbow bolts in a wild volley. One struck Gao Lian squarely in the left shoulder, and their men scattered through the rain to attack. Once Gao Lian had led the spirit soldiers far away, Yang Lin and Bai Sheng, having too few men, dared not pursue them any farther. Presently the rain passed and the clouds dispersed, revealing once more a sky full of stars. By moonlight they found that more than twenty spirit soldiers had been speared down, shot dead, or captured before the grassy slope, and escorted the prisoners to Song Gongming's camp. They gave a full account of the thunder, rain, wind, and clouds. When Song Jiang and Wu Yong heard this, they exclaimed in astonishment, “We are only about five li from there, yet here there was neither rain nor wind!” The men discussed it and said, “Indeed, the sorcery affected only that one place, rising no more than thirty or forty zhang above the ground. The clouds, rain, and vapors must have been drawn over from the nearby marshes.” Yang Lin said, “Gao Lian himself came charging into the camp with his hair loose and a sword in hand. He was struck in the body by one of my crossbow bolts and has gone back to the city. Because we had so few men, we dared not pursue him.” Song Jiang bestowed rewards upon Yang Lin and Bai Sheng. The wounded spirit soldiers they had captured were beheaded. He assigned the chieftains to establish seven or eight smaller camps around the main camp, guarding against another raid, while sending men back to the mountain stronghold to bring reinforcements.
